junction.name: 1st Avenue South & South King Street, Seattle

claims.text: 1st Avenue South & South King Street had 55 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $3.8 million a year.
17% of crashes here were recorded as “parked car” crashes, against 10% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: worked (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.
Lighting would avoid about 1.5 crashes a year (CMF 11027, the median of 2 eligible records), worth $505,000 a year.
Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 0.9 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record), worth $308,000 a year.
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 1st Avenue South, Occidental Avenue South, South King Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
